name: Relay module
author: Bench Workshop
description: A 5 V relay on a module: a board's pin switches a separate circuit (a lamp, a motor, a pump) through its COM, NO and NC contacts. It clicks.

parts.name: Relay module (1 channel)
parts.description: Control side: VCC (5 V), GND, IN. Most modules switch on when IN is LOW (pick in its settings). Load side: COM is joined to NO (normally open) while it's on, and to NC (normally closed) while it's off. The coil takes about 70 mA: more than a pin can give, which is why it's a module (with its own transistor).

examples.name: Relay blinks a lamp
examples.description: A board switches a relay once a second; the relay switches an LED that has its own 9 V battery. Two circuits, one shared nothing: that's what a relay is for.
